newsitem.title: USA: Columbus Energy cancels prfrd rights offer.
newsitem.headline: Columbus Energy cancels prfrd rights offer.

text.p: Columbus Energy Corp said Wednesday it had cancelled plans to raise $10 million in equity through a subscription rights offering to its shareholders after it was able to reduce debt amid a rise in cash flow.

The company said its board of directors voted to withdraw the filed registration statement for 400,000 shares of Series A seven-percent convertible preferred stock with a $25-a-share redemption value.
"(The board) will reconsider what additional funding if any might be required later during 1997 when more results from its budgeted $8 million drilling program are available," it said.
The company said the board's decision was based on "significantly higher" prices for natural gas and crude oil during the last four months.
The completion of new gas wells had also increased natural gas production and subsequent sales revenues, it said.
The company said it was able to reduce bank debt from $3.2 million at the end of August 1996 to $1.6 million in January 1997.
Columbus, which explores, develops and produces crude oil and natural gas, said the board's decision was also influenced by an unexplained weakness in price of its stock at the end of last year.
